question: If I decorate my Python function with @weave.op, will that alone give me the new Agents view with conversations and turns?
answer:
No. The docs treat `@weave.op` as a separate way to trace your code. To get conversations and turns in the **Agents** view, you need to use the Agents tracing APIs or a supported agent integration. The Agents guide says that if you're tracing individual functions as Ops with `@weave.op`, you should use the "Trace LLM applications" guide instead [S1].

**What gives you the Agents view**

- **Agents tracing SDK (code you add yourself):** Weave tracks the agent, its conversations, each turn (one exchange between the user and the agent), the LLM calls in a turn, and the tool calls those LLM calls trigger. Traces appear in the project's **Agents** tab [S1]. You use functions like `weave.start_conversation()`, `conversation.start_turn()`, `weave.start_llm()` and `weave.start_tool()`, usually as `with` blocks, so each record is closed and sent even if an exception occurs [S5].
- **Required setup:** Call `weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")` before any of those start calls. Without it, or when tracing is turned off, the agent tracing functions silently do nothing [S4].
- **Built-in integrations:** Harness plugins group turns into conversations automatically. For supported agent SDKs, `weave.init()` patches the framework, but each call runs only one turn, so your code still has to decide which turns belong to the same conversation. `weave.init()` alone isn't enough [S2].

**Minimal example**

```python
import weave

weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")

with weave.start_conversation(agent_name="[YOUR-AGENT-NAME]") as conversation:
    with conversation.start_turn(user_message="[USER-MESSAGE]") as turn:
        with weave.start_llm(model="[MODEL]", provider_name="[PROVIDER]") as llm:
            llm.output("[MODEL-RESPONSE]")
```

The calls follow the documented pattern [S5]. Add `weave.start_tool(...)` inside the LLM block for tool calls [S5].

# Trace your agents

> Use the Weave SDK to instrument multi-turn agentic applications and view them in the Agents tab.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tracing/instrument.md).

Learn how to instrument a multi-turn agentic application using the W\&B Weave SDK so that you can view, debug, and evaluate your agent's behavior. This guide is intended for developers who build or integrate agents and want structured visibility into conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool executions.

The Weave SDK for Agents models the full lifecycle of a multi-turn agent conversation: the agent that owns many conversations, the conversation that groups turns together, each user-agent exchange (turn), the LLM calls within a turn, and the tool executions that an LLM triggers. Traces appear in the **Agents** tab of your Weave project. Each conversation shows a multi-turn timeline with nested tool calls, token usage, and feedback.

Weave is built on [OpenTelemetry (OTel)](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/), the open standard for distributed tracing. Every turn, LLM call, and tool call emits an OTel *span* (a structured record of one operation). Each span is tagged with [GenAI semantic-convention](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/) attributes like `gen_ai.agent.name` and `gen_ai.conversation.id`.

If you're tracing individual functions as Ops with the `@weave.op` decorator, see [Trace LLM applications](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/tracing.md) instead.

# Choose an agent integration

> Pick a built-in Weave integration for your agent SDK or harness and start sending conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool calls to the Agents view.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/get-started/integrations.md).

W\&B Weave traces multi-turn agents built with popular SDKs and harnesses without hand-instrumenting each turn. Install a plugin for your agent harness, or call `weave.init()` in code that uses a supported agent SDK, and Weave autopatches the framework. Conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool calls render in the **Agents** view of your project.

Harness plugins group turns into conversations on their own, because the harness owns the session. Agent SDKs run one turn per call, so your code decides which turns belong to the same conversation. For those integrations, `weave.init()` alone isn't enough.

Choose from one of the following supported integrations.

No. The docs treat `@weave.op` as a separate way to trace your code. To get conversations and turns in the **Agents** view, you need to use the Agents tracing APIs or a supported agent integration. The Agents guide says that if you're tracing individual functions as Ops with `@weave.op`, you should use the "Trace LLM applications" guide instead [S1].

**What gives you the Agents view**

- **Agents tracing SDK (code you add yourself):** Weave tracks the agent, its conversations, each turn (one exchange between the user and the agent), the LLM calls in a turn, and the tool calls those LLM calls trigger. Traces appear in the project's **Agents** tab [S1]. You use functions like `weave.start_conversation()`, `conversation.start_turn()`, `weave.start_llm()` and `weave.start_tool()`, usually as `with` blocks, so each record is closed and sent even if an exception occurs [S5].
- **Required setup:** Call `weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")` before any of those start calls. Without it, or when tracing is turned off, the agent tracing functions silently do nothing [S4].
- **Built-in integrations:** Harness plugins group turns into conversations automatically. For supported agent SDKs, `weave.init()` patches the framework, but each call runs only one turn, so your code still has to decide which turns belong to the same conversation. `weave.init()` alone isn't enough [S2].

**Minimal example**

```python
import weave

weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")

with weave.start_conversation(agent_name="[YOUR-AGENT-NAME]") as conversation:
    with conversation.start_turn(user_message="[USER-MESSAGE]") as turn:
        with weave.start_llm(model="[MODEL]", provider_name="[PROVIDER]") as llm:
            llm.output("[MODEL-RESPONSE]")
```

The calls follow the documented pattern [S5]. Add `weave.start_tool(...)` inside the LLM block for tool calls [S5].

# Trace your agents

> Use the Weave SDK to instrument multi-turn agentic applications and view them in the Agents tab.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tracing/instrument.md).

Learn how to instrument a multi-turn agentic application using the W\&B Weave SDK so that you can view, debug, and evaluate your agent's behavior. This guide is intended for developers who build or integrate agents and want structured visibility into conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool executions.

The Weave SDK for Agents models the full lifecycle of a multi-turn agent conversation: the agent that owns many conversations, the conversation that groups turns together, each user-agent exchange (turn), the LLM calls within a turn, and the tool executions that an LLM triggers. Traces appear in the **Agents** tab of your Weave project. Each conversation shows a multi-turn timeline with nested tool calls, token usage, and feedback.

Weave is built on [OpenTelemetry (OTel)](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/), the open standard for distributed tracing. Every turn, LLM call, and tool call emits an OTel *span* (a structured record of one operation). Each span is tagged with [GenAI semantic-convention](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/) attributes like `gen_ai.agent.name` and `gen_ai.conversation.id`.

If you're tracing individual functions as Ops with the `@weave.op` decorator, see [Trace LLM applications](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/tracing.md) instead.

# Choose an agent integration

> Pick a built-in Weave integration for your agent SDK or harness and start sending conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool calls to the Agents view.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/get-started/integrations.md).

W\&B Weave traces multi-turn agents built with popular SDKs and harnesses without hand-instrumenting each turn. Install a plugin for your agent harness, or call `weave.init()` in code that uses a supported agent SDK, and Weave autopatches the framework. Conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool calls render in the **Agents** view of your project.

Harness plugins group turns into conversations on their own, because the harness owns the session. Agent SDKs run one turn per call, so your code decides which turns belong to the same conversation. For those integrations, `weave.init()` alone isn't enough.

Choose from one of the following supported integrations.

No. The docs treat `@weave.op` as a separate way to trace your code. To get conversations and turns in the **Agents** view, you need to use the Agents tracing APIs or a supported agent integration. The Agents guide says that if you're tracing individual functions as Ops with `@weave.op`, you should use the "Trace LLM applications" guide instead [S1].

**What gives you the Agents view**

- **Agents tracing SDK (code you add yourself):** Weave tracks the agent, its conversations, each turn (one exchange between the user and the agent), the LLM calls in a turn, and the tool calls those LLM calls trigger. Traces appear in the project's **Agents** tab [S1]. You use functions like `weave.start_conversation()`, `conversation.start_turn()`, `weave.start_llm()` and `weave.start_tool()`, usually as `with` blocks, so each record is closed and sent even if an exception occurs [S5].
- **Required setup:** Call `weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")` before any of those start calls. Without it, or when tracing is turned off, the agent tracing functions silently do nothing [S4].
- **Built-in integrations:** Harness plugins group turns into conversations automatically. For supported agent SDKs, `weave.init()` patches the framework, but each call runs only one turn, so your code still has to decide which turns belong to the same conversation. `weave.init()` alone isn't enough [S2].

**Minimal example**

```python
import weave

weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")

with weave.start_conversation(agent_name="[YOUR-AGENT-NAME]") as conversation:
    with conversation.start_turn(user_message="[USER-MESSAGE]") as turn:
        with weave.start_llm(model="[MODEL]", provider_name="[PROVIDER]") as llm:
            llm.output("[MODEL-RESPONSE]")
```

The calls follow the documented pattern [S5]. Add `weave.start_tool(...)` inside the LLM block for tool calls [S5].

## Multi-turn conversations

Bedrock Agents preserve conversation state on the service side when you reuse a `sessionId`. To group multiple turns into a single trace in the Weights & Biases UI, wrap the turns in `weave.thread`:

```python lines theme={"system"}
with weave.thread("support-conversation") as t:
    for prompt in [
        "I can't log in to my account.",
        "I already tried resetting my password.",
    ]:
        ask_agent(prompt, session_id=t.thread_id)
```

Weave displays each turn in the UI as individual rows in the Threads view.

## How data appears in the Weights & Biases UI

After you instrument your agent with the preceding patterns and run it, your traces appear in the **Agents** tab of your Weave project at `https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb/[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]/weave/agents`.

Learn how to instrument a multi-turn agentic application using the W\&B Weave SDK so that you can view, debug, and evaluate your agent's behavior. This guide is intended for developers who build or integrate agents and want structured visibility into conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool executions.

The Weave SDK for Agents models the full lifecycle of a multi-turn agent conversation: the agent that owns many conversations, the conversation that groups turns together, each user-agent exchange (turn), the LLM calls within a turn, and the tool executions that an LLM triggers. Traces appear in the **Agents** tab of your Weave project. Each conversation shows a multi-turn timeline with nested tool calls, token usage, and feedback.

Weave is built on [OpenTelemetry (OTel)](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/), the open standard for distributed tracing. Every turn, LLM call, and tool call emits an OTel *span* (a structured record of one operation). Each span is tagged with [GenAI semantic-convention](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/) attributes like `gen_ai.agent.name` and `gen_ai.conversation.id`.

If you're tracing individual functions as Ops with the `@weave.op` decorator, see [Trace LLM applications](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/tracing.md) instead.

No. The docs treat `@weave.op` as a separate way to trace your code. To get conversations and turns in the **Agents** view, you need to use the Agents tracing APIs or a supported agent integration. The Agents guide says that if you're tracing individual functions as Ops with `@weave.op`, you should use the "Trace LLM applications" guide instead [S1].

**What gives you the Agents view**

- **Agents tracing SDK (code you add yourself):** Weave tracks the agent, its conversations, each turn (one exchange between the user and the agent), the LLM calls in a turn, and the tool calls those LLM calls trigger. Traces appear in the project's **Agents** tab [S1]. You use functions like `weave.start_conversation()`, `conversation.start_turn()`, `weave.start_llm()` and `weave.start_tool()`, usually as `with` blocks, so each record is closed and sent even if an exception occurs [S5].
- **Required setup:** Call `weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")` before any of those start calls. Without it, or when tracing is turned off, the agent tracing functions silently do nothing [S4].
- **Built-in integrations:** Harness plugins group turns into conversations automatically. For supported agent SDKs, `weave.init()` patches the framework, but each call runs only one turn, so your code still has to decide which turns belong to the same conversation. `weave.init()` alone isn't enough [S2].

**Minimal example**

```python
import weave

weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")

with weave.start_conversation(agent_name="[YOUR-AGENT-NAME]") as conversation:
    with conversation.start_turn(user_message="[USER-MESSAGE]") as turn:
        with weave.start_llm(model="[MODEL]", provider_name="[PROVIDER]") as llm:
            llm.output("[MODEL-RESPONSE]")
```

The calls follow the documented pattern [S5]. Add `weave.start_tool(...)` inside the LLM block for tool calls [S5].
